answer_1.quote: we examine social reasoning capabilities of natural language generation (NLG) models as proxies for intelligent agents navigating social spaces.
answer_1.outputs: The paper addresses NLG tasks involving the generation of normative and divergent actions, consequences, and norms in socially grounded narratives.

answer_2.quote: Generation quality was assessed using a combination of automatic metrics and human evaluation. The former relies on BLEU and ROUGE-L.

answer_4.quote: For models performing best on automatic metrics, human evaluation was conducted by expert workers who contributed at least 25 high-quality stories to the dataset. Each model-generated sample was evaluated by averaging ratings obtained from three different workers.
answer_4.guideline: Raters were asked to assess whether actions are coherent, fulfill the intention, and observe the normative constraint.
